propositions: Link writes are relation-scoped (add_dependency is idempotent per (target_id, relation)) but removal is pair-scoped (unlink takes no relation argument), allowing one ordered pair to hold multiple differently-related deps simultaneously.

When a pair holds two relations (e.g., blocks and relates_to), inbound removal of one relation reaches guard G5 and permanently declines instead of converging because the pair-scoped unlink returns the most-recent link which may not match the vanished relation.

The outbound differ dedupes direction-agnostically on vendor_type (not relation), causing the outbound ADD to be skipped when a local dep's vendor type collides with a remote link of the same vendor type in the opposite direction, leaving no mutation for the inbound differ to suppress and allowing the removal record to survive to G5.

Relation-scoped removal (removal keyed on (target_id, relation)) symmetric with add_dependency is required to make removal convergence symmetric with the write path and symmetric with bidirectional reconciliation.
The CLI and library facade rebar.unlink must gain an optional relation parameter while keeping the no-relation case byte-for-byte pair-scoped for backward compatibility.

Guard G5 must either be unreachable or converge by removing exactly the mirrored relation via relation-scoped removal, with a safety invariant that removes nothing when the named relation has no net-active local link.
